The explanation record, its gate, its authoring and its rendering

packets.title: Measure what a reader sees

gate.red_expect: GATE EX1 RED: the reader-prose measure does not report the fixture's known counts

acceptance: spec.md §1. dev/measure-reader-prose.mjs <docs-dir> prints the JSON shape of §1 with table_chars, prose_chars, table_share and placeholders per page and in totals, by §1's definitions.

The gate builds a three-page fixture in a temporary directory with counts worked out by hand in the test: one page that is all table, one with a fenced block containing '|' characters that must not count as table text, one with two placeholder sentences. It asserts the exact figures, and that a stub returning zeros turns it red.
MEASURE_PLACEHOLDERS is the fixed list of six strings in spec.md §1, defined once in the script and never changed by a later packet; the gate pins the six literals and the list's sha256.

--record <label> appends {label, commit, contract_sha256, placeholder_list_sha256, totals} to the entries array of design/explanation/reader-measure.json, replacing an existing entry with the same label and moving it to the end; this packet records label 'before' over the tracked docs/ and commits the file.
The gate is listed in .github/workflows/test.yml beside the other dev gates and asserts that it is.
No threshold is asserted on the measured figures.
packets.notes: Choices the spec left open: characters are trimmed line length, a table line sums trimmed cell lengths (padding is not text), placeholders are counted anywhere in a page including fenced blocks, and --record takes optional --file/--contract overrides for the gate. 'before' was recorded over docs/ (33 pages, table_share 0.723, 15 placeholders).

packets.title: Render business context and survey notes; the retention gate

gate.red_expect: GATE EX2 RED: a model-authored field reaches no generated page

acceptance: spec.md §2.1. findings.business_context renders as 'Why it matters', after the symptom and before the root cause: a column on the open-findings Markdown table (_finding_table), present for every row and empty where a finding has none; a field on the resolved-findings record list, omitted where empty; and a field on both pages' HTML finding records (html_projection.py, the finding branch and _RECORD_PROJECTIONS), omitted where empty.
vocabulary.expansion renders on the vocabulary page for a term scoped to a subsystem, in the same form render_vocabulary already uses for a codebase-wide term.

subsystems.notes renders under '## Scope' as '### Survey note' with the fixed label sentence, whenever non-empty and whether or not the subsystem has claims or an artifact; the old no-claims fallback under Structure is removed so the notes appear once.

The gate seeds a store in which every field listed in spec.md §2.1 carries a unique sentinel (vocabulary.expansion on one scoped and one codebase-wide term; seams.shared_object and seams.notes included), materializes it, and asserts each sentinel is on at least one page. Follow materializer/test-lens-pages.py for how a fixture store is built from mcp-server/src/schema.sql.

The allowlist holds exactly the eight seam prose columns named in §2.1 (a_writes, a_reads, b_writes, b_reads, ordering_assumption, cardinality, staleness_tolerance, schema_owner), each with its reason, and is two-sided: the gate fails when an allowlisted field's sentinel does appear.
The findings table header literal asserted at materializer/test-materializer.py:465 is replaced by the new header (spec.md §7) and still asserts the full header, not presence.
The gate is listed in .github/workflows/test.yml in the materializer job.
packets.notes: Scoped vocabulary terms now render as ### term records (gloss, expansion, first seen) under 'Scoped to', matching codebase-wide terms; html_projection keeps the old five-column finding signature beside the new six-column one. Gate also asserts HTML records and a second store with empty resolved context; the survey-note fallback under Structure is removed.

packets.title: Claims as a readable register, grouped by recorded segment

gate.red_expect: GATE EX3 RED: a claim's statement does not lead its record

acceptance: spec.md §2.2. Under '## Structure' each claim is a list item whose first text is the statement, with one nested list item beneath it (four-space indent) carrying: claim key in a code span, subject, epistemic kind label, 'asserted at' short revision, and 'evidence:' with the cited files (with ':<line_range>' where evidence.line_range is set, and the role in parentheses where claim_evidence.role is not 'supports') or 'evidence: none attached'.

html_projection.py's list parser gains one level of nesting: an item indented deeper than its list's first item becomes a child <ul> of the preceding <li>. The gate renders the fixture page to HTML and asserts each statement is its own <li> whose coordinates are in a nested <ul>, with no script. Run the whole materializer suite; where an existing page's HTML changes only because its Markdown already nested an item, update that expectation and say so in notes.
No claim has its own heading. mcp-server/test-structural-claims.mjs stays green unmodified.

Grouping follows §2.2: the five recognised segments keep their headings; any other segment is headed by its humanised name ('storage-lifecycle' → 'Storage lifecycle'); 'Other claims' holds only claims whose key is outside the subsystem's '<sid>/' namespace. Group order: recognised kinds, other segments alphabetically, Other claims.

The gate seeds claims with keys '<sid>/recoverability/x', '<sid>/key-type/y' and a key outside the namespace reached through evidence, and asserts the heading each lands under, that the statement precedes the key in the page text, and the evidence text for a claim with a ranged row, an unranged row, a 'contradicts' row and no row.
packets.notes: Evidence rows print in evidence id order and 'asserted at' uses the renderer's existing 12-character _short revision (spec's example says sha8); a statement's whitespace runs collapse so a newline cannot end its list item. html_projection now nests items indented deeper than the list's first item and treats indented ordered items as list items rather than continuation; no existing test expectation needed changing.

packets.title: Survey narrative inside Structure when claims exist

gate.red_expect: GATE EX4 RED: the survey narrative is not inside Structure for a subsystem with claims

acceptance: spec.md §2.3, the two rows with no recorded account. With current claims and a registered survey artifact, the artifact's prose renders inside '## Structure' after the last claim group under '### Survey narrative', led by the existing NARRATIVE_LABEL sentence and the provenance.
'## Survey record' then carries '### Survey artifact' with the one pointer sentence of §2.3 and the provenance; the prose appears exactly once on the page (the gate counts a sentinel).
With no current claim the page is byte-identical to what it is today (row 1); the gate asserts that control against the existing literal heading.
With no artifact, no narrative heading renders.

The recorded-account row is not implemented here: this packet leaves one named helper that decides placement from (has_account, has_claims, has_artifact), called with has_account=False, for EX11 to supply.
packets.notes: Helper is renderers.narrative_placement(has_account, has_claims, has_artifact) returning none/inventory-fallback/structure-narrative/survey-record; subsystem_page calls it with has_account=False for EX11 to supply. Row-1 and no-artifact pages are unchanged; the gate pins the narrative_placement name.

packets.title: File ledger groups rows that share a reason

gate.red_expect: GATE EX5 RED: a reason shared by several ledger rows is printed more than once

acceptance: spec.md §2.4. The subsystem page's file ledger is a list of groups keyed by (classification, why_in_scope), in the existing order; a unique pair is a group of one.

Each group's head line carries the reason in bold, the classification, the file count and a revision label with the short revision. The label is 'examined at' only for classification 'examined' and 'recorded at' for every other classification; with more than one revision in the group it says '<label> <k> revisions' and each path carries its own.

Each path is its own nested list item under the group, keeping its ledger_entry_anchor anchor exactly once; in HTML the paths are a nested <ul> (EX3's nesting). The gate seeds 40 examined rows sharing one reason, two singletons, a candidate group and an exempt group, and asserts: the shared reason appears once; all anchors are present once each; files.md's links still resolve to them; the candidate and exempt groups say 'recorded at' and never 'examined at'; the HTML has one <li> per path.
A row with no reason groups under 'No reason recorded'; a row with no revision prints 'no revision recorded'.
The read-back coverage axis stays green on the fixture (python3 test-readback.py).
packets.notes: Groups are built in _ledger_groups (renderers.py) from the existing ORDER BY classification, file_path, so group order is classification then first path. Heads read 'examined at'/'recorded at'; a multi-revision group says '<label> k revisions' and each path carries (sha8). Anchors render in HTML as span.record-anchor, which the gate matches.

packets.title: Unfilled-slot census and the skill text that feeds it

gate.red_expect: GATE EX6 RED: a rendered placeholder has no census row

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: spec.md §2.5. Materializer.materialize() returns 'unfilled_slots' with rows {slot, page, subject, state, discharge} for the first three slots of the §2.5 table; materialize_docs returns the key unchanged.

For each slot one predicate function returns its state for a subject; the renderer calls it to decide what to print and the census calls it to decide whether to emit a row. The gate asserts, for these three slots, that a row exists if and only if the slot's sentence is on its page, and that a fixture with every slot filled returns an empty list. No other empty-state sentence is a slot.

PLACEHOLDER_SENTENCES is exported from the materializer. The gate asserts each of the six strings in dev/measure-reader-prose.mjs's MEASURE_PLACEHOLDERS occurs in a sentence the materializer can emit; the measure script itself is not changed.

references/onboarding.md names '## What is this codebase?' and '## Runtime boundary map' with its five columns literally where it asks for them; references/phase-5-packaging.md step 5 reads unfilled_slots and fills or reports each row.
The gate asserts parity: THESIS_SECTION_PATTERN matches the heading named in onboarding.md and artifact-templates.md, and the runtime heading and columns in both match what diagrams.py requires.
Nothing halts on an unfilled slot, and no text calls the census a gate or guard.
packets.notes: Census covers thesis, runtime-boundary-map and subsystem-vocabulary via thesis_state, runtime_boundary_state and _vocabulary_state, which the pages also call; PLACEHOLDER_SENTENCES is defined in renderers.py and re-exported from the package __init__.py (not a listed deliverable). The _refused summary omits unfilled_slots because nothing rendered; the gate's no-gate/guard sentence check is sentence-level so onboarding.md's unrelated 'acceptance gate' for entry-point.md is not flagged.

packets.title: The republish chain as one command

gate.red_expect: GATE EX7 RED: the republish chain does not stop before publishing when a tracked path is unledgered

acceptance: spec.md §4.2. dev/republish-docs.mjs runs the ten steps in order as named, injectable functions (preflight, reconcile, freshness, publish, promote, dogfood receipt, depth receipt, progress record, measure, verify); --plan prints them; --from <step> resumes; --measure-label <label> enables the measure step.

Read dev/record-dogfood-receipt.mjs for how a script drives the built server over stdio, dev/promote-docs.mjs and dev/record-survey-depth.mjs for their flags, and `git show 19c8442` for the chain as last run by hand.

With stubbed steps the gate asserts: the order of all ten; that an unledgered path stops the run before publish and names the path; that a dogfood locus (a path named in design/reader-lenses/dogfood-receipt.json) with an owner whose standing is not 'examined' stops it before publish and names the path and owner; that a red read-back or a lint refusal stops it before promote; that the dogfood recorder is never reached without a publish summary; that no reconcile step runs after publish; that the rebuild-* recorders are never invoked; that verify runs last, invokes all four gates of §0.3, and makes the command exit non-zero when any one is red.

The progress-record step rewrites exactly the derived fields §4.2 step 8 names, in end (at_sha, examined, obligation_bearing, fraction) and carried_adjudication (total, decided, to_decide, outcomes, and the successors and repaired lists), from the depth receipt, adds derived_fields_rewritten_at, and leaves every other key byte-identical. The gate runs it on a fixture receipt and fixture progress file and asserts the four relations dev/test-survey-depth.mjs:1278-1330 checks: each outcome count equals its list's length, outcomes sum to the total, the total equals the receipt's carried count, and the end row equals the receipt's coverage.

The publish step writes {commit, unfilled_slots} to design/explanation/unfilled-slots.json; this packet commits that file as {"commit": null, "unfilled_slots": []} so the path exists before the first reconcile.
The script does not guess a subsystem or classification for an unledgered path.
This packet does not run the chain against the live store; EX8 does.
packets.notes: Touches dev/record-survey-depth.mjs, outside the deliverables: B5 rows gain successor_id, since step 8 derives the successors list from the receipt and the receipt had no such field; A1's --check reports drift on blocking until EX8 re-records (already red at baseline). Choices the spec left open: preflight runs npm run build rather than inferring freshness; the census is written only on a green publish; to_decide counts records not archived-terminal, which reproduces the committed 14; state files live in the system temp dir, so no tracked path is added and the primary checkout's git dir is not written; reconcile also stops on absent ledger rows, preflight on an untracked receipt file, promote on an untracked docs page. EX8: commit restore-progress.json before running, as preflight stops on it. Not run against the live store; a scratch copy reached verify.

packets.title: Decide the carried findings, fix the thesis slots, republish, restore the receipt gates

gate.red_expect: GATE EX8 RED: dev/test-reader-lenses-dogfood.mjs is red

acceptance: spec.md §4.3 and §4.4, in that order. You are explicitly authorized to use the Amanuensis MCP tools against this worktree's store for this packet. Call get_project_info with this worktree's absolute path first.

Write the gate first: dev/test-receipt-gates-restored.mjs runs the four gates of §0.3 as subprocesses in the order listed there, prints one summary line of its own per sub-gate and never a child's raw output, and on the first red one prints 'GATE EX8 RED: <its path> is red' with the child's exit code. It also asserts §4.4's file checks, including the CI build step before dev/test-carried-finding-references.mjs, and that reader-measure.json holds 'before' and 'recovered' entries with the last entry bound to the committed docs contract hash.

Create design/explanation/restore-progress.json as {"carried_decided": 0, "records": []} before deciding anything, and commit it. After each carried record is decided, append its id and outcome and increment carried_decided, and commit. If the budget runs out, set status=blocked with the reason and stop; the launcher resumes you.

Each of the 14 undecided carried records gets exactly one terminal outcome through record_carried_outcome, decided by reading the code it names at HEAD (§4.3's table). Evidence is attached to every outcome. No outcome is chosen to clear the gate.

Then §4.4: rename the thesis heading in the store's entry-point.md, add the runtime boundary map table to onboarding-report.md, rehash both; ledger every unledgered tracked path with add_files_to_scope (this lane's files included, classified by the convention their neighbours use); run `node dev/republish-docs.mjs --measure-label recovered`. When it stops at the freshness step, re-examine each named locus: read the file at HEAD, record the examination at HEAD through the ledger tool, clear its staleness, and rerun the script. Never clear staleness on a file you have not read; leave other stale rows stale.
Add no tracked path after the script's reconcile step: every file written after it already exists. Commit docs/ and the receipts together in one commit.
In .github/workflows/test.yml, add npm ci and npm run build for mcp-server before the carried-finding references step in its job.
The gates named in spec.md §4.1's second table are not this packet's; do not re-record a rebuild-* receipt.
If the chain script has a defect, fix it and extend EX7's gate with the case that would have caught it.
packets.notes: Outcomes: 10 successor, 4 repaired, 0 ruled out. Successor ids avoid every live and archived id; B03-R6 records that 8 ids already collide and a Pecia reference resolves wrongly. B05-R1 is repaired though a green publish can still carry the placeholder, per spec 2.5. Deviation: 15 of 21 newly ledgered paths are candidate, not their neighbours' examined, because this session did not read them in full. Gate reads Why it matters as the table column spec 2.1 defines.

packets.title: The explanation record: schema, enums, effective-row reader and two writers

gate.red_expect: GATE EX9 RED: record_explanation is not refused for a subsystem that is not explanation-eligible

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: spec.md §3.1–§3.3, the two writers only (get_explanations and the reset rule are EX15). Copy the vocabulary declination pattern end to end: mcp-server/src/schema.sql (vocabulary_declinations and its two triggers), contracts/append-only-tables.txt, src/tools/vocabulary.ts (decline_domain_vocabulary), src/invariants.ts (readVocabularyDischarge), the ADDITIVE_TOOLS entry in src/index.ts, and mcp-server/test-vocabulary-discharge.mjs for the gate's shape.
Tables explanations and explanation_evidence exactly as §3.1 (stored dispositions recorded, declined, withdrawn), append-only, created on open of an existing store.

conspectus-vocabulary.json gains explanation_subject, explanation_slot and explanation_disposition, each with the generator's `sql` binding to its explanations column, and explanation_discharge (recorded, declined, not-recorded) with no sql binding; every value has label, meaning and cannot_justify. subsystem_status values gain the boolean explanation_eligible (true for structural, concerns, adversarial, mapped). Regenerate both vocabulary modules with scripts/gen-vocabulary.mjs; extend the generator only as far as the new boolean field needs.

readExplanation in invariants.ts implements §3.2 around a pure selection function over (rows, resolvable revisions, eligibility). contracts/explanation-effective-cases.json holds the shared cases §3.2 lists, each with its expected state and row id; the gate runs the selection function over every case.

record_explanation raises each of R1–R8 with the message stem in §3.3's table and accepts a valid purpose and account; decline_explanation applies the conditions of R1–R4 with its own stems beginning 'decline_explanation refuses:', plus the 400-byte and one-paragraph rules on the reason. A successful write returns only {id, subject_type, subject_id, slot, disposition, ref_sha}.

The gate drives the built server and asserts: every refusal by its stem; the byte caps at the boundary (400 and 401, 4096 and 4097, and the reason cap); that UPDATE and DELETE on both tables raise; that a second row at the same commit becomes effective; that a row with an unreachable ref_sha is skipped; that the write response is the same size for a ten-byte body and a body at the cap; that a set mixing a ledger file with outside files is accepted (R7).
No minimum length and no evidence count above one is enforced; the gate records a ten-byte purpose with one evidence row and expects success.

Every refusal sentence of both tools is registered in contracts/refusal-parity.json with references/explanations.md as its reference; create that reference with a 'Tools' section giving each tool's use and its refusal phrases (EX10 adds the content brief). scripts/check-refusal-parity.mjs and test-refusal-parity.mjs pass.
The tool inventory and schemas are regenerated (scripts/gen-tool-inventory.mjs) and every checker in the regression list passes.
materializer/test-prose-retention.py gains explanations.body in its seeded fields with the allowlist entry 'rendered by EX11', so EX2's gate stays green; EX11 removes the entry.
mcp-server/src/tools/locus.ts is not modified.
packets.notes: attempt 1 was marked done but the launcher refused it: VERIFY EX9: red output does not match gate.red_expect (GATE EX9 RED: record_explanation is not refused for a subsystem that is not explanation-eligible)

references/explanations.md's Tools section gains get_explanations; the tool inventory and schemas are regenerated.

packets.title: The mapped gate, refusal parity and the authoring instructions

gate.red_expect: GATE EX10 RED: a subsystem reached mapped with neither a purpose nor a declination

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
acceptance: spec.md §3.4. requireExplanationDischarge in invariants.ts refuses every status write whose target is 'mapped' and whose current status is not 'mapped', unless the effective purpose and the effective account are each recorded or declined. It is invoked on its own path by both status writers (mcp-server/src/tools/subsystems.ts), not only inside the `case "mapped"` branch, since assertStatusTransition and enforceForwardPrerequisites both return early for a transition from 'deferred'. The message is §3.4's, naming what is missing.

The gate drives both status writers and asserts: refused with neither slot; refused with only one; allowed with two records; allowed with two declinations; allowed with one of each; refused from 'deferred' with neither slot and allowed from 'deferred' with both, through each writer; a write that leaves a 'mapped' subsystem 'mapped' is not checked; an advance to 'adversarial' is not gated; without a bound workspace a slot with a row proceeds with a report that its revision was not resolved, and a slot with no row is refused.

Every existing test whose fixture moves a subsystem to 'mapped', from any status, gains declinations through one shared fixture helper. Find them by running the whole mcp-server test directory and dev/test-*.mjs before and after; no assertion is removed or relaxed, and the set of tests green before this packet is green after it.
The refusal is registered in contracts/refusal-parity.json and quoted in references/phase-5-packaging.md; test-refusal-parity.mjs stays green.

spec.md §3.5. references/explanations.md is the content brief with the purpose, subsystem account and project account as specified, and the rules for all three; SKILL.md lists it; each row of §3.5's phase table is applied to its reference, with get_explanations named as the way the adversarial, packaging and refresh phases read what was recorded.
The skill text sets no length floor and says declining with a reason is a complete answer.

packets.title: Subsystem page leads with Purpose and How it works

acceptance: spec.md §3.6. Section order: '## Purpose' only when the effective purpose is recorded or declined; '## Scope' always; '## Start here'; '## How it works' only with a recorded account; then Structure onward.

Not-recorded state: the page is what it is today, opening with '## Scope' and the NO_PURPOSE sentence. materializer/test-lens-pages.py keeps its assertions for that state and gains a control that a Purpose heading never renders without a record (spec §0.2, §7).
Recorded and declined states render the texts of §3.6; in both, '## Scope' prints no disclaimer; scope is never relabelled.

Every rendered explanation carries the provenance line; the ageing sentence is computed per §3.6's table. The gate builds a temporary git repository, records an explanation citing two files, commits a change to one, and asserts the three sentences: none changed, one of two changed with its path, and not measured when the revision does not resolve.

A recorded body or declination reason with an orientation-lint violation is not printed, the refusal sentence takes its place and the publish fails. core.py passes the failure callback (warn=self._warn, as it does for render_index) to render_subsystem. With a recorded account the survey narrative renders under '## Survey record' whatever the claim count (§2.3); the gate seeds a recorded account with current claims and with none; EX4's gate stays green.

packets.title: Explain pass over the self-conspectus and the final republish

gate.red_expect: GATE EX14 RED: a surveyed subsystem page has no Purpose section

regression: cd mcp-server && npx biome check src/
